transcript.speaker: Farshad Soleimani
transcript.text: Good night, everyone. Welcome to the Digital Workflow Optimization Initiative. Management calls it a project. I call it a cry for help. We are here to fix the boring glue holding us together while the company's on fire.

transcript.speaker: Mobin
transcript.text: Is this the one where we optimize without knowing what that means?

transcript.speaker: Farshad Soleimani
transcript.text: Exactly, documentation, tracking, communication, the works.

transcript.speaker: CHRISTINE MATHEW VATHIYATH MATHAI
transcript.text: Can we start with the documentation? Last week's note literally said budget maybe, action item wipes.

transcript.speaker: Safa V Abdul Ravuf
transcript.text: And the files guys, I found the onboarding checklist in a folder named do not delete, delete on a random desktop. That's digital archaeology.

transcript.speaker: Adarsh Haridas
transcript.text: The spreadsheets are haunted too. I opened one and Excel crashed like it was protecting state secrets.

transcript.speaker: Tabia Karim
transcript.text: The UI is basically mad at you for using it. If it takes more than three clicks to find a task, it's a crime.

transcript.speaker: Ananthu Vijayan
transcript.text: Management wants numbers without KPIs, we just optimize it until we die.

transcript.speaker: Mobin
transcript.text: I think the real lick is the digital bucket brigade. Meeting happens, notes go somewhere, tasks go maybe on Trello, if you remember.

transcript.speaker: Farshad Soleimani
transcript.text: Okay, stop. I'm one person. We need owners because everyone owns it means no one does.

transcript.speaker: Mobin
transcript.text: I'll map the manual steps to the end to end the copy paste suffering.

transcript.speaker: CHRISTINE MATHEW VATHIYATH MATHAI
transcript.text: I think I prefer standardized templates, templates no more writing notes like we are texting.

transcript.speaker: Safa V Abdul Ravuf
transcript.text: I can do a predictable storage system, no more discovering new civilization every time we search for a PDF.

transcript.speaker: Adarsh Haridas
transcript.text: No garbage allowed pipeline, if it's a duplicate or outdated, it gets flagged.

transcript.speaker: Tabia Karim
transcript.text: I will prioritize simplification so we can reduce clicks and I need help messages.

transcript.speaker: Ananthu Vijayan
transcript.text: Dashboard for time saved plus a matrix for how many times we had to resend the link.

transcript.speaker: Mobin
transcript.text: We talk for 40 minutes and forget everything immediately.

transcript.speaker: Farshad Soleimani
transcript.text: I don't forget. Okay, I forget instantly. I'm like a goldfish with Outlook.

transcript.speaker: Safa V Abdul Ravuf
transcript.text: an AI handles the transcript, summary, and reload pipeline, you might stop losing data.

transcript.speaker: Adarsh Haridas
transcript.text: We can filter the noise, translate we should maybe consider exploring into no task, just anxiety.

transcript.speaker: Ananthu Vijayan
transcript.text: And the dashboard proves to management this is just a fancy notepad.

transcript.speaker: Farshad Soleimani
transcript.text: Okay, so the milestones are for the next week, we draft plans and sample templates from everyone. And in two weeks, we need an end-to-end pilot meeting using the AI workflow. And the target is to 30% reduction in manual admin efforts.

transcript.speaker: Mobin
transcript.text: 30%? Is that real or aspirational?

transcript.speaker: Ananthu Vijayan
transcript.text: It's a number that makes management come, so it's real.

transcript.speaker: Adarsh Haridas
transcript.text: We are the Avengers, the villains are spreadsheets.

transcript.speaker: Farshad Soleimani
transcript.text: Great. Okay. Great. For next week, we need updates, templates, workflows, a structure map, KPI definitions. Oh, God, I wish I had an assistant who could organize this mess in my head.

summary: - The Digital Workflow Optimization Initiative meeting was aimed at addressing inefficiencies in documentation, tracking, and communication within the company.****- Farshad Soleimani emphasized the need for ownership, highlighting that when everyone owns a task, no one does.****- Major issues discussed included disorganized documentation, inconvenient task management systems, and a lack of standardized procedures.****- Several team members shared their experiences with the current system, likening the disorganization to digital archaeology and haunted spreadsheets.****- Suggestions for improvement included implementing standardized templates, a predictable storage system, and reducing the number of clicks needed to complete tasks.****- Responsibilities were assigned: Mobin will map manual processes, Christine will develop standardized templates, Safa will create a storage system, Adarsh will manage the pipeline, and Tabia will focus on simplifying user interfaces.****- Ananthu proposed a dashboard for tracking time saved and addressing task completion metrics.****- The team plans to utilize AI for automated transcription and summaries to prevent data loss.****- The initial milestone is to draft plans and sample templates within the next week, with an end-to-end pilot meeting using AI workflows scheduled for two weeks later.****- The aim is to achieve a 30% reduction in manual administrative efforts, though there is skepticism about whether this is a realistic goal.****- Farshad expressed the need for updates, templates, workflows, a structure map, and KPI definitions for the following week's meeting.

tasks.descr: Map out all manual processes in the workflow to identify areas of inefficiency. Reference process mapping resources and Six Sigma basics to guide your analysis.
Using your automation expertise, create a comprehensive map of the current end-to-end process. Refer to BPMN diagrams from 'bpmn.io'.
Draft a preliminary project plan using Microsoft Project. Reference 'The Fast Forward MBA in Project Management' for best practices.
Outline key performance indicators for the project. Use 'Key Performance Indicators: Developing, Implementing, and Using Winning KPIs' as a guideline.
Set up an automated workflow using n8n. Utilize n8n docs and GitHub examples to integrate triggers and actions effectively.
Conduct tests on the newly created automated workflow. Follow best practices like those in the 'Testing JavaScript Applications' book for assurance.
Prepare detailed documentation illustrating the differences pre- and post-automation. Use resources such as the Microsoft Word documentation guide.
Develop standardized templates for documentation and notes. Refer to Microsoft's 'Get Started with Document Templates' guide for ideas.
Organize existing files into a systematic storage system using cloud services. Follow Google's Drive storage best practices.
Create a pipeline to flag duplicate or outdated data entries. Refer to data management principles outlined in 'Data Science for Business'.
Prioritize simplifications in UI to reduce click complexity. Use Jakob Nielsen's Usability Heuristics as a reference for improvements.
Design a dashboard to track time saved from optimizations. Apply concepts from Stephen Few's 'Information Dashboard Design'.
